songs.title: Billie Jean
songs.description: Iconic 1980s dance-pop milestone engineered by Bruce Swedien at Westlake Studios. Features custom drum isolation, Acusonic stereo mic pairs, Harrison 3232 console summing, and minimalist analogue compression.

criteria.name: Capture
criteria.question: True or False: Identify the valid capture techniques used in Billie Jean.

answers.text: Leon Ndugu Chancler's drum kit was recorded on a custom wooden platform raised off the studio floor to eliminate floor resonance and low-end bleed.
answers.reason: Correct: Bruce Swedien built an 8x8 foot wooden drum riser for this exact purpose.

answers.text: Michael Jackson's lead vocals were tracked using a Shure SM7 dynamic microphone with the windscreen removed and a custom pop filter.
answers.reason: Correct: Swedien famously tracked MJ's vocals with a Shure SM7 dynamic microphone.

answers.text: The kick drum was baffled with a heavy blanket and a custom wooden sound pipe to isolate the direct mic from the snare and cymbals.
answers.reason: Correct: Swedien used a custom-built kick drum cover to isolate the kick transient.

answers.text: The lead vocals were recorded with an omnidirectional boundary mic placed on the studio glass window.
answers.reason: Incorrect: A Shure SM7 dynamic cardioid mic was used.

answers.text: All instruments were captured live with zero multitrack overdubs onto a 2-track reel-to-reel tape recorder.
answers.reason: Incorrect: Billie Jean utilized synchronized twin 24-track tape machines (48 tracks total).

answers.text: The kick drum EQ boosts the sub-bass fundamental around 50-60 Hz and adds a sharp presence boost around 3.5 kHz for beater click.
answers.reason: Correct: Swedien shaped the kick drum to have sub weight and transient punch.

answers.text: Low-mid frequencies (300-500 Hz) were carefully cleaned and notched out on secondary parts to prevent mix muddiness.
answers.reason: Correct: Swedien prioritized clarity and separation by decluttering low-mid frequencies.

answers.text: A high-shelf boost was applied to the hi-hat and shaker tracks to enhance sparkling 10 kHz+ top-end shimmer.
answers.reason: Correct: High frequencies were accentuated to cut through dense rhythm arrangements.

answers.text: A 50 Hz steep high-pass filter was applied to remove all sub-bass from the kick drum and bassline.
answers.reason: Incorrect: The sub-bass in Billie Jean was preserved to drive club sound systems.

answers.text: An extreme mid-range telephone filter was placed across the entire stereo master mix.
answers.reason: Incorrect: The master mix exhibits full-frequency commercial fidelity.

criteria.name: Dynamics
criteria.question: True or False: Identify the dynamic processing techniques used in Billie Jean.

answers.text: Bruce Swedien deliberately avoided using master mix bus compression to preserve wide dynamic punch and transient clarity.
answers.reason: Correct: Swedien was famous for not compressing the master mix bus to preserve natural transients.

answers.text: Individual percussion and bass elements used subtle outboard dynamic control, including a dbx 160 compressor on the bass guitar.
answers.reason: Correct: Outboard VCA compression was used selectively on individual tracking channels.

answers.text: An optical leveler (LA-2A) was used on Michael's vocal overdubs to gently smooth dynamic fluctuations.
answers.reason: Correct: Smooth optical leveling was standard in Swedien's Westlake vocal chain.

answers.text: The entire mix was heavily brickwall limited to -6 LUFS using digital lookahead limiters.

answers.reason: Incorrect: No aggressive gating chatter is present in the organic mix.

answers.reason: Correct: The EMT 250 digital reverb was used extensively on the snare drum at Westlake.

answers.reason: Correct: Short tape slapback and Lexicon digital reverberation gave MJ's vocal spatial dimension.

criteria.question: True or False: Identify the historical and technological context of Billie Jean.
